raw_case_text:
A 67-year-old woman, with a history of arterial hypertension, diabetes mellitus type II, thyroidectomy, osteoporosis, hyperlipidemia and rheumatoid arthritis being treated with methotrexate and corticosteroids, presented to our Pulmonology Department in August 2019 with progressive dyspnea at rest and fatigue over the last two days. 
Clinical examination revealed an afebrile patient with crackles on auscultation at all lung fields. Blood pressure was 100/80 mmHg, heart rate was 120 beats per minute, oxygen saturation was 79% on room air and body temperature 36.5  C on admission. Electrocardiography showed sinus tachycardia. Arterial blood gas analysis revealed pO2 40mmHg, pCO2 35mmHg, pH 7.48 and HCO3  29.2 mmol/L on room air. Chest X-ray showed patchy diffuse infiltrates in both lungs mostly in the left lower lobe (Figure 1A).
Complete blood count was normal. The blood biochemistry parameters and thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) were normal, with the exception of an elevated serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) 311 U/L (normal <225 U/L), serum glycose 263 mg/dl (normal 60-100 mg/dL) and C-reactive protein (CRP) 122.3 mg/L (normal <6 mg/L). Urinalysis was normal. 
The reversed transcription polymerase chain reaction (RTau-PCR) test for Influenza A and B in nasopharyngeal and oropharyngeal samples were performed and were negative. Urinary antigen tests for Legionella pneumophila and Streptococcus pneumoniae, serological testing for Mycoplasma pneumonia and blood cultures were negative. 
The patient received oxygen therapy with Venturi mask delivering 60% oxygen and intravenous antibiotic therapy with ceftriaxone, azithromycin and trimethoprim-sulfomethoxazole empirically. After the first two days of hospitalization the patient presented with respiratory deterioration and diffuse lung infiltrates (Figure 1B), was intubated and admitted to intensive care unit.
Computed tomography (CT) of the chest was performed. Chest CT revealed diffuse ground glass opacities in all lung fields (Figure 1C, 1D) and bilateral pleural effusion (Figure 1E, 1F). The patient underwent echocardiography with normal ejection fraction and valve function. Bronchoscopy was performed and bronchial washings and bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) were obtained from lingula and right middle lobe. Cytological and microbiological examination of bronchial washings and BAL was negative. Direct immunofluorescence and PCR for Pneumocystis jirovecii in BAL were negative and administration of trimethoprim-sulfomethoxazole was discontinued. Respiratory virus panel test in BA for detection of human respiratory viruses by use of multiplex RT-PCR was performed and revealed HCoV-HKU1. 
The patient after five days of intubation presented with improvement, was extubated and received oxygen therapy with Venturi mask. The patient had gradually completely recovered without any specific therapy. She denied recent travel or contact with a person that had recently returned from a travel abroad.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 67-year-old woman on methotrexate and corticosteroids for rheumatoid arthritis presented in August 2019 with a 2-day history of progressive resting dyspnea and fatigue.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient, who was receiving methotrexate and corticosteroids for rheumatoid arthritis, presented to the pulmonology department with rapidly progressive shortness of breath at rest and fatigue over the preceding 48 hours. She denied recent travel or sick contacts.
subjective.past_medical_history: Rheumatoid arthritis treated with methotrexate and corticosteroids; arterial hypertension; type 2 diabetes mellitus; status post thyroidectomy; osteoporosis; hyperlipidemia.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for resting dyspnea and fatigue for 2 days; negative for fever. Home medications included methotrexate and corticosteroids.

objective.physical_examination: Admission vital signs: Afebrile (36.5 °C), blood pressure 100/80 mmHg, heart rate 120 beats/min, and room-air SpO2 79%. Chest auscultation: Diffuse crackles across all lung fields bilaterally.
objective.routine_investigations: Room-air arterial blood gas: Severe hypoxemia with pO2 40 mmHg, pCO2 35 mmHg, pH 7.48, and HCO3- 29.2 mmol/L. Laboratory tests: Normal CBC, electrolytes, renal/liver function, TSH, and urinalysis; elevated serum LDH at 311 U/L (normal <225 U/L), blood glucose 263 mg/dL (normal: 60–100 mg/dL), and C-reactive protein (CRP) 122.3 mg/L (normal <6 mg/L). Negative baseline microbiology: Negative nasopharyngeal/oropharyngeal influenza A/B RT-PCR, negative urinary Legionella pneumophila and Streptococcus pneumoniae antigens, negative Mycoplasma pneumoniae serology, and negative blood cultures. ECG and echocardiography: Sinus tachycardia with normal left ventricular ejection fraction and valve function. Serial chest X-rays: Patchy bilateral infiltrates (predominantly left lower lobe) progressing to diffuse bilateral infiltrates on day 2.
objective.advanced_workup: Chest CT scan (hospital day 2): Diffuse ground-glass opacities across all lung fields and bilateral pleural effusions. Bronchoscopy with bronchial washings and bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) from the lingula and right middle lobe: Negative bacterial/fungal cultures and cytology; negative BAL direct immunofluorescence and PCR for Pneumocystis jirovecii; multiplex respiratory virus RT-PCR panel on BAL fluid tested positive for human coronavirus HKU1 (HCoV-HKU1).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Severe human coronavirus HKU1 (HCoV-HKU1) pneumonia causing diffuse ground-glass opacities and acute hypoxemic respiratory failure in an immunocompromised patient with rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate and corticosteroids, definitively diagnosed by BAL multiplex RT-PCR after excluding Pneumocystis jirovecii by BAL direct immunofluorescence and PCR. Plan and clinical course: Initially managed with 60% Venturi mask oxygen and empiric IV ceftriaxone, azithromycin, and trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, then intubated on hospital day 2 for progressive respiratory failure. Following negative BAL P. jirovecii DFA/PCR and positive HCoV-HKU1 detection, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole was discontinued; she improved with supportive ICU care, was extubated after 5 days to a Venturi mask, and achieved full recovery.
